We show that the language-modeling loss scales as a power law with model size, dataset size and training compute, with some trends spanning more than seven orders of magnitude.
We find that performance depends strongly on scale and weakly on model shape, and that every 8x increase in model size needs only about a 5x increase in data to avoid an overfitting penalty.
Under a fixed compute budget, the best performance comes from training very large models and stopping well before convergence.
